results.title: Luv FM’s Clinton Yeboah wins Best Radio Feature at 30th GJA Media Awards
results.content: Luv FM journalist Clinton Yeboah has won the Best Radio Feature award at the 30th Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Media Awards held in Accra on November 7, 2026. The award recognises his work in radio feature production and adds to a series of honours he has received for his journalism. Earlier in 2026, Mr Yeboah won two first-place awards in the Health and Business/Economy Journalism categories at the GJA Ashanti Regional Media Excellence Awards. The latest recognition extends his award record across different areas of journalism.

results.title: GJA calls for better pay and conditions to protect media independence
results.content: The Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) has called for improved remuneration and working conditions for journalists, warning that poor welfare threatens media independence and professional integrity. President of the Association, Albert Dwumfour, said the economic conditions under which many journalists work continue to undermine the dignity and independence of the profession. Speaking at the 30th GJA Media Awards in Accra, he identified poor remuneration, insecure employment, inadequate conditions of service, irregular salary payments and limited opportunities for professional development as persistent challenges facing media practitioners. “Poor remuneration, insecure employment, inadequate conditions of service, irregular salaries, and limited opportunities for professional development continue to undermine the dignity and independence of journalists,” he said.

results.title: GJA criticises Sam George over comments on media closures and engagement with Mahama
results.content: The Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) has criticised the Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George, over comments suggesting that its President, Albert Dwumfour, sought President John Dramani Mahama’s intervention following the minister’s remarks about shutting down politically and religiously affiliated media organisations. Mr Dwumfour described the comments as unfortunate, insisting that the Association has a responsibility to speak out whenever the rights, welfare and livelihoods of journalists are threatened. results.title: Bagbin assures GJA of support for bill on journalists’ conditions of service
results.content: Speaker of Parliament Alban Bagbin has assured the Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) of Parliament’s readiness to support the development of a private member’s bill to address the conditions of service of journalists and other media practitioners. GJA President Albert Dwumfour disclosed this at the 30th GJA Media Awards in Accra, saying the assurance followed a recent engagement between the Speaker and the Association. “During our recent engagement with the Right Honourable Speaker of Parliament, Alban Sumana Kingsford Bagbin, Mr Speaker gave the association an important assurance of Parliament's readiness to partner the GJA in developing a private member's bill to address the conditions of service of journalists and media practitioners,” he said. Mr Dwumfour described the assurance as a significant commitment towards improving the welfare and professional dignity of journalists.

results.title: Ghana to host Federation of African Journalists Conference in 2027 – Dwumfour
results.content: Ghana will host the Federation of African Journalists (FAJ) Conference in the first quarter of 2027 after the Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) secured the bid, its President, Albert Dwumfour, has announced. Speaking at the 30th GJA Media Awards in Accra, Mr Dwumfour said the successful bid was among a series of continental achievements recorded by the Association in the past four years. He also cited Ghana's successful bids to host the African Media Convention and the FAJ Steering Committee Meeting as part of efforts to strengthen the country's influence in Africa's media landscape. “Within the past four years, the Ghana Journalists Association has chalked up significant continental achievements, further elevating Ghana's profile and influence in Africa's media landscape,” he said.

results.title: ‘Journalists are not enemies of the state’ – Dwumfour urges respect for press freedom
results.content: President of the Ghana Journalists Association (GJA), Albert Dwumfour, has called for greater respect for press freedom, insisting that journalists are not enemies of the state amid persistent attacks and harassment of media practitioners. Speaking at the 30th GJA Media Awards in Accra, he said the Association had recorded more than 50 incidents involving attacks, arrests and harassment of journalists between 2022 and January 2026. “Journalists are not enemies of the state,” he stated. Mr Dwumfour said Ghana's progress in international press freedom rankings should not overshadow the challenges journalists continue to face in carrying out their work.

results.title: GJA records more than 50 attacks and threats against journalists since 2022
results.content: The Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) says it has recorded more than 50 incidents involving attacks, assaults, arrests, threats and harassment of journalists between 2022 and January 2026. President of the Association, Albert Dwumfour, disclosed this at the 30th GJA Media Awards in Accra, where he raised concerns about the safety of journalists despite progress in Ghana's press freedom ranking. He said five attacks were recorded in January 2026 alone, with three allegedly involving state security personnel. “Journalists are not enemies of the state,” he stated.

results.title: GJA President warns against complacency despite Ghana’s improved press freedom ranking
results.content: President of the Ghana Journalists Association (GJA), Albert Dwumfour, has cautioned against complacency following Ghana’s rise to 39th out of 180 countries in the 2026 World Press Freedom Index. He said the improved ranking should not overshadow persistent challenges facing journalists, including safety concerns, economic insecurity, threats to media independence and the need for professional development. Speaking at the 30th GJA Media Awards in Accra, Mr Dwumfour said Ghana had moved up from 52nd in 2025 and 62nd in 2023, placing fourth in Africa, according to the latest index published by Reporters Without Borders (RSF). He attributed the improvement to sustained advocacy, institutional commitment and engagement among stakeholders. “This improvement reflects the importance of sustained advocacy, institutional commitment, and engagement among stakeholders,” he said.

results.title: Leveraging pension power: How Ghanaian trade unions can turn capital into Worker rights
results.content: Globally, organised labour is navigating an unprecedented structural crisis. Membership densities continue to dwindle, undermined by expanding informal economies, shifts in employment relationships like casualisation, and subtle to aggressive corporate anti-union practices. In response, the international labour movement under the guidance of the International Trade Union Confederation (ITUC) has continuously urged affiliated unions to innovate, revise, and modernise their organising and recruitment strategies. Still, while unions in Ghana search for new ways to recruit workers, they often miss one of their most cogent levers: the financial power of public sector workers’ pension funds. results.title: The barcode and the brown notebook
results.content: Walk into any of the sprawling red-and-yellow department stores along the Spintex Road or the Tema motorway on a Saturday afternoon. The first thing that strikes you is the quiet. Nobody is shouting over the price of a blender. Nobody is sizing up your shoes to decide whether to quote you two hundred cedis or three hundred and fifty. A mother pushes a metal trolley past towering shelves of plastic bins, LED bulbs, and silicone kitchenware. Every item wears a printed barcode. At the till, a young Ghanaian cashier scans the label. The point-of-sale terminal chirps, a thermal receipt rolls out, and the customer steps back into the heat. Three kilometres away, inside a traditional stall at Makola or Ashaiman, a very different transaction unfolds.

results.title: IOTA Leadership Dealership 2026 challenges young people to become solution-driven leaders
results.content: Africa’s growing youth population presents a major opportunity for the continent, but persistent unemployment, weak institutional accountability and rapid technological change are raising questions about whether young people are adequately prepared to shape its future. With millions entering the labour market, speakers at the second Leadership Dealership Conference organised by the IOTA Ministry Groupe have urged young Africans to develop the values, skills and sense of responsibility needed to lead in an increasingly complex world. The conference brought together speakers from business, technology and faith to examine the character, competence and discipline required for impactful leadership. results.title: Medical Superintendents call for stronger emergency care to tackle no-bed syndrome
results.content: The Medical Superintendents Group is calling for an expansion of emergency and critical care facilities, alongside improvements in hospital referral systems, to address Ghana's persistent no-bed syndrome. The group says tackling the problem will require political commitment, sustainable financing and stronger collaboration among healthcare institutions. Speaking at the 68th Annual General Conference of the Ghana Medical Association (GMA), a representative of the group said hospital managers experienced the challenges associated with the no-bed syndrome firsthand. “Where we sit, we experience, firsthand, all the challenges associated with the no-bed syndrome,” the representative said.

results.title: Journalism educators from 10 countries to meet in Accra for disinformation conference
results.content: Journalism educators and media professionals from 10 countries across the Sahel and West Africa will meet in Accra from November 11 to 13 for a conference focused on tackling disinformation and strengthening information integrity. The inaugural STREAC Autumn School will examine media and information literacy, information manipulation and the growing impact of artificial intelligence on journalism and journalism education. The three-day event will be held at the La Palm Royal Beach Hotel and feature workshops, research presentations and discussions among participants.

results.title: Eisenkot to be tasked with forming next Israeli government
results.content: In a setback to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, his main rival will be tasked with forming the next Israeli government, placing him one step closer to ousting Israel’s longest-serving leader, even as the path remains complicated.
